intro: Edward Neeman plays Chopin’s Étude in G♯ minor, Op. 25 No. 6 (“Thirds”), which Chopin marked sotto voce — in an undertone. A right-hand trill leads into scales of paired notes, and the left hand plays a slower melody.

sections.label: A · Trill in thirds, right hand
sections.mNote: The right hand opens playing two notes at a time.

sections.label: B · Left-hand melody beneath right-hand thirds
sections.mNote: The left hand plays a slower melody beneath the right-hand thirds.

sections.label: C · Thirds climb and descend
sections.mNote: The right hand plays its paired notes in smooth succession.

sections.label: Coda · Closing bars in thirds
sections.mNote: The running thirds continue into the study’s closing bars.

cues.title: Opening trill in thirds
cues.text: The right hand opens with a trill in thirds, each movement shifting two notes together. The pairs then run up and down in chromatic scales. Beneath them the left hand plays a slower melody, which Chopin marked sotto voce.
cues.evidence: Opening trill, scales and the hands’ relationship: Fred Yu, https://www.ourchopin.com/analysis/etude25.html. Sotto voce marking: Mieczysław Tomaszewski, https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/192.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Neeman’s sostenuto mechanism
cues.text: Neeman developed a change to the sostenuto mechanism that allows a pianist to combine it with the damper pedal in new ways. He presented the results to teachers and performers.
cues.evidence: Australian National University biography describes Neeman’s innovation to the sostenuto mechanism and presentations at the MTNA National Conference and Australian National Academy of Music. https://music.cass.anu.edu.au/people/dr-edward-neeman

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
